import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Jacobson Conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobson's_conjecture)
- [He1965]: Herstein, I. N. (1965), "A counterexample in Noetherian rings",
  Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America, 54 (4): 1036–1037
  https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC219788/
- [Ja1956]: Jacobson, Nathan. Structure of rings. Vol. 37. American Mathematical Soc., 1956.
- [Le1977]: Lenagan, T. H. (1977), "Noetherian rings with Krull dimension one",
  J. London Math. Soc. Series 2, 15 (1): 41–47
  https://londmathsoc.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1112/jlms/s2-15.1.41
-/

open Ring

universe u

namespace Jacobson

/-- The Jacobson conjecture for a ring $R$: the infimum of the powers of the Jacobson radical
$J$ is the zero ideal. -/
def JacobsonConjectureFor (R : Type u) [Ring R] : Prop :=
  ⨅ n : ℕ, jacobson R ^ n = 0

/-- The Jacobson conjecture (in its modern form):
In a (noncommutative) ring which is left and right Noetherian,
the intersection of the powers of the Jacobson ideal is trivial -/
@[category research open, AMS 16]
theorem jacobson_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (R : Type) [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsRightNoetherianRing R],
      JacobsonConjectureFor R := by
  sorry

/-- For commutative rings this is the case as a consequence of Krull's intersection theorem. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 13 16]
theorem jacobson_conjecture_of_comm_ring (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] :
    JacobsonConjectureFor R := by
  sorry

/-- Originally, on page 200 of [Ja1956], Jacobson asked if the Jacobson conjecture holds for all right
Noetherian rings. However in [He1965] Herstein constructs a right Noetherian ring for which the
Jacobson conjecture does not hold. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 16]
theorem jacobson_conjecture_of_right_noetherian :
    answer(False) ↔ ∀ (R : Type) [Ring R] [IsRightNoetherianRing R], JacobsonConjectureFor R := by
  sorry

/- In [Le1977] Lenagan shows the Jacobson conjecture holds for left and right Noetherian rings
with Krull dimension $1$. -/
-- TODO: Add this result. Note that we do not have Krull dimension for noncommutative rings yet.

end Jacobson

reformulations.difference: Uses an infimum in the lattice of left ideals, equal to the zero ideal, rather than a set intersection of powers of the two-sided Jacobson radical equal to {0}.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Ring.jacobson is the intersection of maximal left ideals and is two-sided. Its ideal powers use ordinary ideal multiplication, ideal infima have set intersections as their carriers, and the zero ideal has carrier {0}. The exact equivalence with the source's set-intersection formulation was proved in scratch. Including n = 0 is harmless because J^0 is the full ideal; this was also proved.

reformulations.difference: Encodes Herstein's counterexample result as `answer(False) ↔ ∀ R [Ring R] [IsRightNoetherianRing R], JacobsonConjectureFor R`, rather than explicitly asserting existence of a counterexample.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Classically, `False ↔ ∀ R, P R` is equivalent to existence of an admissible R with ¬P R. Here failure of the zero-intersection property is equivalent to existence of a nonzero element belonging to every radical power. This entire equivalence, including the ring and right-Noetherian instance quantifiers, was proved in scratch.

sources_consulted: I. N. Herstein, "A counterexample in Noetherian rings", PNAS 54 (1965), 1036–1037; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC219788/ (including OCR of both scanned pages).

K. A. Brown and T. H. Lenagan, "A note on Jacobson's conjecture for right Noetherian rings", Glasgow Mathematical Journal 23 (1982), 7–8; https://doi.org/10.1017/S0017089500004729 (abstract and full PDF).
https://archive.org/metadata/structureofrings0000jaco (catalogue/access metadata for a later edition of Jacobson's book, not its text).

Local definitions: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/RingTheory/Noetherian/Defs.lean and RingTheory/Ideal/Defs.lean; Mathlib's Noetherian/Defs, Jacobson/Radical, Jacobson/Ideal, Ideal/Operations, Algebra/Module/Opposite, Algebra/Algebra/Operations, and RingTheory/Filtration modules.
review.notes:
Checked the definition and all three theorems. The left/right Noetherian hypotheses, answer scopes and polarities, and recorded statuses agree with the sources. Scratch checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile without errors or warnings and without relying on the reviewed sorry theorems. They include the equivalences above, a proof of the commutative special case from Mathlib's Krull-intersection theorem, zero-ring and finite-ring cases, and a noncommutative matrix-ring case. A computable check also confirms that 2 is a nonzero radical element in ZMod 4, so the definition is not identically zero.

Direct access to Jacobson's book and Lenagan's 1977 full text was unavailable. Brown–Lenagan explicitly confirms the original right-Noetherian question and the page-200 attribution, while Herstein directly supplies the counterexample and poses the two-sided version. Lenagan's result is only mentioned in an unformalized TODO, whose description agrees with Wikipedia; no Lean declaration depends on verifying its detailed hypotheses.
